chunks: Verily God's is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He alone is the giver of life and death; and none do you have besides God as friend and helper.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God has the kingdom of the heavens and the earth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores Tawhid al-Mulk (Divine Sovereignty), affirming that all authority and agency ultimately derive from Allah, a concept central to understanding the Imamate as the manifestation of His will on earth. It serves as a theological foundation for reliance (Tawakkul) on God alone, distinguishing between true divine support and the transient aid of created beings. This reinforces the Shia belief that while Imams are guides, they are not independent sources of power but conduits of Allah's grace.
